claims.assertion: The trip ran 20.1 km against an optimal 15.5 km, a deviation of +4.6 km (+30%), which exceeds the 1 km RD-1 tolerance.

No rider-requested stop or route exists to exempt the segment: no place or road was named by the rider, and the driver's late statement does not meet the mutual-agreement requirement.

Without a traffic reason, the outcome is a partial refund of the excess distance fare plus a recorded driver violation; the refundable amount is the billed excess of $6.50 (4.61 km at $1.4099/km), and the excess distance charge is the refundable component only (tolls, time fare and surge are excluded, and surge here is 1.0x).
Because the driver failed to inform the rider, the driver should also receive a notification-duty reminder logged on his route-compliance record (no formal warning for a first such incident).
The driver has 3 upheld route deviations in the last 90 days, so a repeat-deviation account flag is warranted; his profile is used only for that add-on, not for the finding.

Nothing in the record proves the driver's motive; the judge may treat the Paya Lebar exit as an ordinary navigation decision rather than a deliberately uninformed reroute, though RD-4 still supplies no traffic justification (F8, F12).

Conceded on consent; the chat record holds no messages at all (F7) and the driver's 'I followed my GPS' statement (F8) is post-trip, so RD-5 notice and RD-3 agreement both fail. This is why my own brief does not contest the excess-distance refund, only its scope.
Conceded; with no rider message (F7) no place or road is named for the segment (F3), so the F3 ground is consent_after_or_none.

Conceded that the refundable figure is the billed excess distance fare of $6.50 (F4, 4.61 km × $1.4099/km at 1.0× surge per F5), which is exactly what I ask for; the rider's complaint about 'almost 20 km' cannot enlarge it into the time fare (F6).

The reminder under RD-7 attaches to a refund for not informing the rider and is a compliance-record entry, not an additional money claim, so it does not change the amount; I note the rider's advocate must still prove this is a first such incident, since the driver's record shows 3 upheld route deviations in 90 days (F15).

A flag_account under RD-6 is an add-on and does not decide this case; the profile (F15) never decides the finding, and the rider's own profile is neutral with 1 dispute and 0 upheld (F14), so credibility points neither way.

I do not withdraw D6: the honest outcome on this record is refund_partial of the $6.50 excess distance fare (F4) with a violation recorded under RD-2, which is what both advocates now ask for; the only live difference is that the refund cannot reach the $8.84 time fare or $1.47 platform fee (F6).

notices.text:
We looked into your trip and found the driver took a detour that was not justified by traffic or weather. Your route was 20.1 km versus the 15.5 km best route, and one stretch between 12:46 and 13:07 added 4.08 km that was billed to you.

We're refunding $6.50 — the extra distance fare — back to your original payment method. It should appear within a few business days depending on your bank. The time fare, platform fee and any surge charges are not refundable and stay as billed.

You don't need to do anything else. Thanks for flagging this.

We reviewed the route on this trip. It ran 20.1 km against a 15.5 km best route, and one stretch between 12:46 and 13:07 covered 9.70 km where the best route is 5.62 km. Traffic and weather don't account for it, and the rider wasn't told before or during the detour, so the excess $6.50 is being refunded to the rider.

This is logged as an unjustified reroute on your route-compliance record. You're also getting a reminder about your duty to tell the rider when you deviate from the best route. It's a first incident, so no formal warning this time. Because you have repeat route deviations in the last 90 days, a flag has been added to your account. Please follow the best route and let riders know about any changes.
